findings.limit: Calling a new mixed protocol a held-out check does not make it independent if final code fits it. The new response still relies on approximate manually stated parameters.
findings.positive: Matched a previously acquired constant-input prefix, inserted an idle interval, and proposed pointwise comparison to the original continuation. A correct recovery contrast in principle.

findings.limit: Earlier delta between a resumed point and approximate prediction does not establish a recovery upper bound0.005 smaller than one-point noise0.015. Several residual-based mechanism suspicions use selected noisy outliers and approximate k~0.0825 rather than a numerical joint fit.
findings.positive: Three protocols match integrated input10 and duration40 before an identical readout tail; observed first tail values0.731145,0.725907,0.748706 support dose invariance against the proposed flux-driven alternative.

findings.limit: The later Latin-square slots are no longer exactly state-matched, because earlier test inputs differ. At round4 the model ignored its own round3 matched reference (u0.2 y20=0.148023 vs u1 y20=0.353560) and treated only the adjacent-time comparison as confounded.
findings.positive: Three identical ten-second prefixes followed by different test inputs at t10 give a valid matched-state readout contrast. Observations u1:0.706981,u0.4:0.526931,u0.15:0.312043 favor the proposed separable readout.

findings.limit: The readout pulses at u0.3 are not non-invasive: state evolves under u0.3 during each pulse. A correct prediction must include them. Similar responses under a finite collection of tests cannot prove unique state dimensionality or a chemical mechanism.
findings.positive: Proposed approach to the same intermediate-input regime from above and below, and a deep depletion/recovery experiment. This asks a structural question beyond parameter tuning.

findings.limit: Its displayed working equation uses g normalized to g(1)=1 without the1.634 amplitude, while later predictions restore that amplitude. Several numerical rival predictions are only approximate. Claims that one rest rules out all recovery are broader than evidence.
findings.positive: Uses observed fresh amplitude and decay-rate ratios to reject linear input scaling and distinguish input-driven depletion from flux-driven depletion.

findings.limit: Its saturation readout predictions omit normalization: matching y1=1.634 and K0.35 gives y0.1~0.490, not the stated0.36. A later response corrects the working saturation amplitude using actual measurements.
findings.positive: Recovery protocols have identical five-second depletion prefixes followed by two- versus fifteen-second rests. Returned first-on outputs1.230981 and1.578655 provide a useful matched contrast with the previous five-second rest.

findings.limit: Its claimed flux-driven alternative at u0.75 predicts >0.8, but using its own rates and normalized saturating flux predicts roughly0.52. Sequential low-input samples after a common depletion prefix are not all at a common state; a proportional pattern alone cannot prove multiplicative readout.
findings.positive: Explicitly rejects input-independent recovery because it predicts a high-u plateau inconsistent with the already observed low and declining output. States the correct input-suppressed recovery functional form as the working hypothesis.

scope: Independent scientific interpretation of acquired results only. Not passed to any research model and not used to alter its proposals. Final programs require separate reviews.
